The Evil Within is one of those fondly looked back upon games that just didn’t do it for me. It attempted to cram together every horror genre out there—psychological, surrealism, action, survival—all of which are done better in other games. Sure, there were a few memorable sequences, but the constant jumping around resulted in a disjointed experience. Add to that the convoluted way of storytelling, and well, I just wish I had loved it as much as most.
What I did like included certain environments and boss fights. Don’t get me wrong, it looked good, artistically speaking. In the beginning I even enjoyed myself, but it overstayed its welcome and by the end I couldn't help but hate it.

The Evil Within is a super polarizing game. There are very interesting environments, but as soon as you get to them, it feels like they take it away and replace it with a super generic horror environment (Ex: sewers). It seems like that is the point of the game, but it would've made it phenomenally better if they allowed some exploration around these environments. 

The next thing the game does well is... the journal entries? Let me explain, you can get various tidbits of lore from journal entries scattered around the world. There is your characters journal which is written really well and I would look forward to finding them. There are also various notes you can find scattered around that are written by other people that give a small bit of information about what happened in the many different environments you find yourself in. These are cool and give insight to the greater mystery in the story. Also they are about the only way to minimally understand the story, so there's that. 

Also I liked some of the character designs I guess. The bosses are cool to look at, at least most of them (Looking at you Keeper, you knock off Pyramid Head ass). But most of the time you are fighting fodder enemies that get annoying upgrades. More on this later. 

That is about all I liked about the game. Honestly, I have seen reviews stating the game is a masterpiece at horror and I do not understand why. Literally the only tension in the game is at the very beginning when you have no weapons and need to stealth around enemies. Around chapter 2 (out of 15 chapters) the game becomes an action shooter that is disguised as a horror game. You get a lot of different weapons and plenty of ammo. The game becomes a shooting gallery. The problem with this is, you don't know when to fight, and when to run. There are a few segments where you need to lead a mini-boss through a level instead of killing it. I specifically remember one part where I was supposed to do that, but didn't. I was able to "kill" the thing, and it disappeared. I looked around the area and looted it but when I got to the cutscene trigger the thing just respawned for the sake of the cutscene. I understand that it needed to be there for the scene, but please give me better signs when I am supposed to run away instead of fighting. 

The game controls are garbage. They are a weird combination of tank controls and controls you would expect from a 2015 game. It feels so clunky. There were plenty of times I have been hit by traps I was trying to defuse because my character cannot inch forward. This could just be a me thing, but I hated it. 

Most of the characters are garbage. Your main guy, Detective Sebastian Castellanos, is a turd. He really has no emotion whatsoever. He is a bland protagonist in a story that is crazy. The only reason I like this character is because of his journal entries. Those things give him more emotion than the entire game. He is boring, he is also supported by the most boring sidekick ever: Detective Joseph Oda. He is a bookworm. That's it. That is about all he gets. Then there is Detective Juli Kidman. She would be cool if she actually got some development. She is missing 90% of the game and when she shows up, she just says some cryptic shit and leaves. There are other characters that are just as generic and stupid, but the best ones are Leslie and Ruvik. They actually get some decent character development IN THE STORY and you start to understand why Ruvik is doing the things he is. It gives the villain motivation. 

Difficulty in this game is awful. Oh my god is it bad. The game itself is not hard, you can kill most enemies with a few shots and you most definitely will be. But then it throws in enemies and bosses that have one shot moves. WHY? It cheapens the whole experience to just get hammered immediately when you enter a boss room. It's not hard, and there is no tension, just my burning rage every time I have to retry this damn boss. Fodder enemies get these annoying upgrades to just piss you off. THEY GET GUNS! These guns take a sizable chuck of your health. Not to mention, they get assault rifles, and by god they don't miss. Hope you like getting stunlocked to death. Oh, they also get plate masks that block your bullets from headshotting them, so that's fun. Then there are what I like to call "gimmick rooms". These are rooms where they are full of traps, that instant kill you, and you have to maneuver through them. Sounds simple right? Wrong. There is always some sort of thing in the room to mess up your movement, whether it be a roomba-saw (yes, you read that right) or the shitty camera. When you are in enclosed spaces the camera just freaks out. Trying to do something when the camera is giving me a close up of Sebs back is not ideal or fun. 

The story. Where to begin about the story. I didn't hate it. It was interesting once you get to about chapter 6. From there it starts to pick up and get good. But there are just so many dumb moments throughout it that don't really make sense. Well, the whole thing doesn't really make sense to begin with I guess. Just a warning, when you play this you will have no idea whats going on until about 3-4 hours in the game. While the story is interesting, it is hard to get engrossed in it. 

In conclusion, The Evil Within has some interesting ideas, but drops the ball with everything else. I am sure there are things I have forgotten to include, but I think this review is long enough. I swear this game was an experiment to see how much shit we can throw at a person until they just accept it and turn their brain off. Oh the last boss is a turret section. That's just awesome. 

I would not recommend this game.

Rating: 8/10
Genre: Third Person Shooter/Survivor Horror 

The Good: 
+ Great graphics

+ The game does a great job of mixing up the environments, enemies, gameplay scenarios throughout the 15 chapters. It does a good job of making sure nothing feels repetitive.  

+ Conserving ammo and item management is crucial for survival. Luckily, the game has multiple ways of killing enemies such as using stealth and/or the environment.  

+ Bosses are disgusting, grotesque and feel satisfying to beat. 

+ The DLC content is excellent, providing, all new gameplay scenarios, environments and enemies.  The 2 DLC’s ‘The Assignment and ‘The Consequence’ provide more backdrop to the story and help explain things a bit better in the main game. 

The Average: 
+/- Certain game mechanics are not explained properly or completely ignored. The game vaguely mentions burning enemies to keep them dead but as far as I could tell, that isn’t true at all.  Another minor gripe, in one of the early chapters, a character says he will distract the enemies while you try to open a gate. So naturally, I thought that after he distracted the enemies I would run up and open the gate only to find out you must kill most enemies in the area to proceed. 

+/- The story seems to thrust you into the action with little to no explanation or care. Non-of the characters seem to question what is happening and just accept everything happening around them. However, as things progress, more of the characters motives are revealed and things begin to make more sense.  

+/- For those looking for a frightening, scary game, I am not sure you will find it here. As grotesque as the game is, I was never truly scared, I am not sure its because I have played so many of these games before or the game itself but judging from other peoples opinions, it seems to be the game.

The Bad:
- Sticking to 30 FPS is probably the best option as going higher seems to result in unstable framerates and glitches. 

Conclusion:
I am very surprised by the low Metacritic score, as this game is a fantastic game and well worth at least a single playthrough.  There were times where I felt like I was playing a modern-day Resident Evil 4.

If you get caught, you are dead, and have to return to a checkpoint that was probably forever ago. The Keeper boss fight is just frantically running around turning valves on a timer, you can't actually kill the thing but the game sure makes sure you waste your ammo before you realize that. Amalgam Alpha has an attack that one shots you. I didn't know that it was easy to avoid until I looked it up in a guide later. (Might be my fault) ((Probably my fault)). There's a boss fight in a freezer room with an arena so obnoxious. You get stuck on the meat hanging constantly. The double keeper bossfight was awesome though. Unique arena, plenty of space and ammo and a chance to learn the arena beforehand was really nice. But the final boss is so awful, it's just a turret section. You shoot at designated areas and then the head and it dies.

The story is a giant mess, honestly couldn't tell you much about what happened if I wanted to. Even after looking it up I couldn't make any sense of it, and the character motivation just didn't exist really. I even had a friend who had played the first AND the 2nd and he still couldn't explain what happened.

The performances are incredibly subpar with Yuri Lowenthal providing the best performance as Joseph Oda, a genuinely nice helper to have around. The main character is not likable in the slightest. Just another beat-cop (detective) cliche character. He says random things randomly and all of his backstory is found in little exposition notes at given save points that are boring and pointless to read. Reading after that he was originally supposed to be a blank slate definitely shows. You have a main character named Juli Kidman who has absolutely zero emotion in her voice. Couldn't care less about her or Sebastian basically the entire game. The main villain's voice actor definitely doesn't help in trying to make him sound any more threatening.

The environments in this game seem to be pretty widely praised by people but I just don't get how. The color pallete is just brown and gray and sometimes red. I can get behind the gross environment thing but the game just gets awful to look at. Some very poor design decisions as well with some not just artistically. There's a room near the end of the game in chapter 13 or 14 I believe that has nearly invisible traps, fire, and a bunch of saw roombas, including an area at the end where you are just left to fate as the roombas may or may not swipe you as you do a really long defusing segment.

The A.I is a mess as well. Bosses will have attacks that have no room to maneuver hardly, like the Neun and Zehn boss in Chapter 6 (which is awful and takes forever but that's not something I'll get into) where he attacks over and over and over and over in a tiny cramped little space and you are basically forced to get hit by an attack that doesn't ever seem to end. On the companion A.I side, there were several times (most of the time) where Joseph would just sit there and do nothing as an enemy attacked me. He just seemed to run around without having any sense of direction which was annoying when you are getting swarmed by enemies.

I have to wrap this up at some point but if you want a subpar horror game with a confusing and overall badly told story, bad ai, good enemy design, and higher blood pressure, this game just might be for you! Please be aware that the Negative recommendation reflects the current price point of the title and not the overall quality of the game. 
 
 
The Evil Within did as most well advertised games do.  It rode the hype train all the way to its release.  People boarded, they drank and ate frivolosly as they spoke of their excitement for the title amongst themselves (Myself included) But when the train arrived at a concentration camp and we were herded out to a firing line and systematically shot, we began to complain.  Is it our fault?  Of course it is, but all the blame does not fall upon us alone.  The Evil Within as a whole is not a "Bad" game.  Several hours of entertainment can be found within, but for those expecting to be swept up into a AAA horror look elsewhere.  
 
Poor ports seem to be the bread and butter of the porting scene.  This game, although playable, is poorly optimized for its PC consumer base. A "widescreen" picture (Two large horizontal black lines at the top/ bottom of the screen) that can not be removed without some small degree of tech savvy file modding) takes away from the overall gameplay.  Frame locked to any degree is a sure fire way to piss everyone in the PC world off, and a windowed mode that doesn't truly allow for "Windowed mode" are just a few things on the list of recommended things to be altered, improved, or altogether removed. 
 
Some may argue that issues arise with all games and to that I agree, to an extent.  There are simply too many variables to be able to cover all issues for all the varying degrees of hardware/software out there.  However, things like locked frames, although many say this issue is self fixable, should not be released in a AAA title with a price tag of 60 dollars.  Others will express that the fixes will come in time and to be patient.  To them I give a hearty, fuck you.  Order a pizza dinner for 40 bucks have it show up three hours later and be the completely wrong order to which the proprietor of the establishment, after you are forced to call or suffer through the wrong order, tells you they will remake your order and send it out to you....most likely in another three hours.  Would you not be upset?  The concept is the same. 
 
Is The Evil Within fun?  Mostly 
Is it playable?  Yes. 
Did it make good on its promises?  It didn't make any, it's a game. 
Has it lived up to the "Hype" it received?    No. 
 
Recommendation.  Wait for it to go on sale.
